item.title: MySQL Stored Procedures vs. Functions: Choosing the Right Approach
item.description: In MySQL, both stored procedures and functions are powerful tools for encapsulating logic on the database server. However, they serve different purposes and have distinct characteristics. This article aims to clarify the differences between MySQL stored procedures and functions and helps you decide when to use each in your database development. MySQL Stored Procedures: Stored procedures are a collection of SQL statements that can be executed as a single unit. They can include control-flow constructs such as loops and conditionals.
